lead.headline: Houthis Say They Struck the Pipeline That Lets Saudi Oil Avoid Hormuz
lead.deck: Reuters reports the group's claims on Monday; Saudi Arabia has not confirmed them.
body: Saudi Arabia sends much of its oil out through one sea lane, the Strait of Hormuz at the mouth of the Gulf. That lane has been largely shut by the war, so a Saudi pipeline now matters more. The East-West pipeline is about 1,200 kilometres long and gives Saudi crude a route to the Red Sea coast instead.

On Monday the Houthis, an armed group from Yemen, said they hit the pipeline's crude pumping stations and Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport. They made similar claims on Saturday, naming an Aramco site in Yanbu and the Rabigh refinery. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation. The airport had reopened two terminals on Sunday, after an attack earlier this month that Reuters says killed 13 people.

The Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed two ballistic missile launchers in Sanaa, Yemen's capital, and five tunnels used to store missiles. Houthi media say Saudi strikes killed 16 people, a figure that could not be checked. Strikes have intensified since the Houthis captured strategic areas on Yemen's Red Sea coast last month, moving towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key route for Gulf oil. The fighting has effectively ended a UN-brokered truce that had largely held since 2022.

For families, the link is the pump. The American Automobile Association (AAA) says the average US price was $4.28 a gallon on Sunday. India buys much of its oil from abroad, and its Sensex share index rose 482.92 points on Monday as oil prices eased, after four days of falls.

world.headline: Israel Votes With Neither Side Near a Majority
world.deck: The final polls point to deadlock, and Arab parties could decide who governs.
body: Israel holds a parliamentary election on Tuesday 27 October. Unlike in the United States, voters do not pick a prime minister directly. They choose parties for the 120-seat parliament, the Knesset, and the leader who can build a governing coalition becomes prime minister. A coalition is a group of parties that agree to govern together, and it needs 61 seats.

The final polls from three TV channels give Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing and religious bloc 50 seats. They give the opposition 'change bloc', led by former defence chief Gadi Eisenkot, between 52 and 56. Eisenkot's party, Yashar, is projected as the largest with 22 seats, ahead of Netanyahu's Likud with 20. One poll by Direct Polls, quoted by i24NEWS, put Netanyahu's bloc at 59.

Security shapes the vote. NBC News describes it as a battle for survival for Netanyahu after the attacks of 7 October 2023. Israel will close West Bank crossings on election day, and Netanyahu has been pressing US President Donald Trump for more support before a tight race. Ynet reports that the final polls put Eisenkot's party ahead of Likud.

Small parties could matter too. The Kan poll puts Amcha Israel at 2.9%, below the electoral threshold, the minimum share of votes a party needs to win any seats. Votes for a party that falls short win no seats at all, which can change the arithmetic of both blocs.

Neither camp reaches 61, and that is why the Arab parties matter. They are projected to win 14 to 16 seats and are counted in neither bloc. Coalition talks could be hard, and another election is possible if no government forms.

india.headline: Cyclone Arnab Gathers Strength Before Its Landfall
india.deck: Odisha shuts schools and Andhra Pradesh waits for winds of up to 125 km an hour.
body: Cyclone Arnab is still over the sea. At 5:30pm on Monday, India's weather office said it was a severe cyclonic storm about 490 kilometres east-south-east of Visakhapatnam, and expected it to become a very severe one within 12 hours.

The office forecasts that it will cross the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, near Yanam, by the forenoon of 28 October. Winds at the coast could average 115 to 125 km an hour, with gusts to 140. A red-message warning covers the Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts. The rain is expected to continue into 29 October and ease from 30 October.

For families on the coast, the preparations are practical. Schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres close in five Odisha districts on 28 and 29 October. Odisha has 302 rescue teams on standby, and 225 fire service teams and NDRF personnel have been deployed. Fishing is suspended, and more than 4,800 boats have returned to the Kakinada coast.
india.why: Fishing families lose a day's earnings when boats stay in, but warnings given early are how coastal India keeps people safe.
also: Name: Bangladesh proposed 'Arnab', which means 'sea' or 'ocean' in Bengali.

us.headline: One Week Before the Midterms, Early Voting Spreads
us.deck: Obama and Trump both campaigned in Michigan, and Fox News lists six Senate toss-ups.
body: Election Day for the midterms, the vote halfway through a president's term, is 3 November. It decides whether Republicans keep control of the House and the Senate. Millions have already voted: AP data published on 17 October showed 6 million early votes across 39 states.

This week more states open early voting. It starts in Washington DC on Monday, in Oklahoma on Wednesday and in Kentucky on Thursday. Barack Obama rallied in Cleveland and Detroit on Saturday, and Donald Trump campaigned with Republican Mike Rogers in Port Huron, Michigan, on Sunday.
Fox News lists Alaska, Iowa, Maine, Michigan, Ohio and Texas as toss-up Senate states. Its Power Rankings predict Republicans would still lose the House even with a good showing.

world.headline: Israel Holds a Close Election
body: Israel votes on Tuesday for a parliament of 120 seats. Voters pick parties, not a prime minister. The leader who can get 61 seats together becomes prime minister.
The last polls say neither side will reach 61. One side is projected to get 50 seats. The other is projected to get between 52 and 56.
Arab parties could win 14 to 16 seats. That could decide who forms the government.

india.headline: A Big Storm Is Coming to India's Coast
body: A cyclone is a huge spinning storm over warm sea. This one is called Arnab. It is expected to reach Andhra Pradesh on 28 October.
Winds could gust up to 140 km an hour. Schools will close in five districts of Odisha. Odisha has 302 rescue teams ready.
Fishing has stopped. More than 4,800 boats have come back to the coast.

us.headline: Early Voting Grows Before US Elections
body: The US holds midterm elections on 3 November. People can vote early in many states.
By 17 October, 6 million people had voted early across 39 states. This week, Washington DC, Oklahoma and Kentucky start early voting.
Fox News lists six Senate races as toss-ups. That means either party could win them. Many people are watching these races, because they help decide who controls Congress.
